subject.title: [Bug]: Native Codex subagents silently fall back from ChatGPT OAuth to API-key billing

question: Does private/current-main evidence show that a subscription-selected Codex run can transition to API-key billing without selecting an explicit ordered API-key profile?
rationale: Current OpenClaw source and docs prohibit the reported ambient-key takeover, while the billing evidence and matching upstream report indicate a real credential-boundary failure that cannot be safely attributed without sensitive logs and usage data.

options.title: Privately reproduce and trace
options.body: Reproduce on current main with an instrumented effective-auth trace and compare request timestamps against the redacted Platform export before changing the credential boundary.

options.title: Treat as upstream Codex defect
options.body: If OpenClaw proves the app-server receives only OAuth credentials, route the minimal reproduction and billing correlation to https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/20099 while retaining OpenClaw telemetry improvements.

options.title: Disable all API fallback
options.body: Make subscription-selected runs unconditionally OAuth-only, accepting that this would remove the currently documented ordered API-key backup behavior.

recommendation.title: Privately reproduce and trace
recommendation.body: Reproduce on current main with an instrumented effective-auth trace and compare request timestamps against the redacted Platform export before changing the credential boundary.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the central environment isolation and auth-profile rotation behavior most directly implicated by this report.
